Note::hex_decode¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::hex_decode() const

Decode Every Cell From Hexadecimal¶

hex_decode() is the inverse of hex_encode: it reads each cell as a run of hex digit pairs and replaces it with the decoded bytes. Both lowercase and uppercase digits are accepted. Use it to unpack a value that was carried as hex.

The decoded bytes go into a UTF-8-mode Note as-is. For any Note produced by hex_encode() this is an exact round trip. Decoding is lenient: it does not raise on stray non-hex characters or an odd digit count — it decodes what it can. Do not use it as a validator.

The operation is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note; an empty cell decodes to an empty cell.

Example 1: Decode A Batch¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"486921", "636166c3a9"}).hex_decode())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["Hi!", "café"]

Example 2: Exact Round Trip¶

const pluss::Note original = pluss::make_note({"Hi!", "café"});
std::cout << original.hex_encode().hex_decode() << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["Hi!", "café"]
